question: What does Brutus mean when he says to Cassius “No more, I pray you.” In Act IV Scene 3?
options: He is requesting Cassius to yield to the second triumvirate
He is pleading to Cassius for not stabbing him
He is requesting Cassius to not speak about Portia’s death anymore
He is requesting Cassius to let Messala speak now
explanation: Brutus restrains his emotions and asks Cassius to stop speaking about Portia’s death.

question: What is the significance of “A hot friend cooling”?
options: Love after some time begins to sicken and decay
When a friend starts to drift apart, he/she assumes forced civility to us
One of our friends, who had been suffering from fever was now fine
None of these
explanation: It refers to a friendship losing warmth and turning into formal politeness.

question: Why does Brutus decide to march to Philippi?
options: He thought that Sardis was a plain area hence very unsafe
He wanted to act as a superior authority to Cassius
He believed that Sardians had grudged contributions to them
He thought that it would be really unpredictable for Antony and the team
explanation: Brutus believes attacking early will prevent Antony and Octavius from gaining strength.

question: What is meant by “rash choler”?
options: Unpredictable behaviour
Nasty and cranky temper
Hasty and fiery temper
Sudden shift to infuriation
explanation: ‘Choler’ refers to anger; ‘rash choler’ means quick-tempered anger.

question: What was the difference in the letters received by Brutus and those received by Messala?
options: Messala’s letter said that Portia was alive unlike Brutus’ letter
Different number of deaths of conspirators
Messala’s letter mentioned Antony and Octavius preparing for battle, unlike Brutus’ letter
Both b & c
explanation: Messala’s letter reveals political and military details that Brutus conceals or already knows.

question: With reference to the Ghost of Caesar, select the correct statement:
options: The ghost could possibly be a manifestation of Brutus’ underlying guilt
The ghost is a metaphor for how powerful Caesar is
The ghost is a reflection of Brutus’s past indiscretions
Both a & b
explanation: The ghost represents both Brutus’ guilt and Caesar’s enduring influence.

question: What does Octavius mean by “Never, till three and thirty wounds of Caesar be avenged or till another Caesar adds slaughter to the sword of traitors”?
options: Octavius’s sword will not come down until Brutus dies
Octavius’s sword will not come down until all Caesar’s wounds are avenged
Octavius’s sword will not come down until he adds to the slaughter
Both b & c
explanation: Octavius vows continuous violence until Caesar’s murder is fully avenged.

question: Brutus: “But this same day must end that work the Ides of March begun.” What does that work mean?
options: Never ending warfare
Destruction & bloodshed
Caesar’s death
Antony’s rise to power
explanation: The ‘work’ refers to Caesar’s assassination which began the chain of events.

question: Cassius: “… get higher on that hill, my sight was ever thick.” To whom does Cassius say this?
options: Messala
Pindarus
Titinius
Lucilius
explanation: Cassius asks Pindarus to climb higher and observe the battlefield.

question: What does Titinius mean when he says “Our day is gone”?
options: Night is approaching and they are about to lose
They will all die by night
Their time of happiness and fortune has ended
Cassius has finally died
explanation: It symbolizes the loss of luck and the turning of fortune against them.

question: Why does Messala blame error for Cassius’ death?
options: Error is born from melancholy and leads to false conclusions
Cassius’s judgements were always full of errors
Error was responsible for Cassius’s sadness
Error killed Cassius’ mother
explanation: Cassius misinterprets the situation due to emotional confusion.

question: What is Brutus trying to do when he says “Yet, Countrymen, O, yet hold up your hands!”?
options: He is asking them to surrender
He is motivating and encouraging his soldiers
He is asking them to applaud Cassius
He is ordering them to fight endlessly
explanation: Brutus is rallying his troops and boosting their morale.

question: Who is the speaker of: “And I am Brutus, Marcus Brutus, I, Brutus, my country’s friend.”?
options: Lepidus
Messala
Lucilius
Cato Jr.
explanation: Lucilius pretends to be Brutus to protect him.

question: Whom does Brutus ask to send Cassius’ body to Thasos?
options: Claudio
Labeo
Messala
Volumnius
explanation: Brutus entrusts Messala with the responsibility.

question: Who is the speaker and listener of “Fellow, wilt thou bestow thy time with me?”?
options: Octavius, Messala
Messala, Strato
Octavius, Strato
Strato, Messala
explanation: Octavius addresses Messala after the battle.

question: What is the significance of Brutus’ final speech “Farewell to you, you and you…”?
options: Brutus is leaving for Rome
Brutus wants to give up temporarily
Brutus is ready to die and end his life
None of these
explanation: The speech signals Brutus’ acceptance of death before committing suicide.
